nodes.norm_label: callable type analysis and attribute inference prototype

nodes.label: Cumulative qualitative issue triage
nodes.rationale: Overlapping impact categories, current evidence, readiness, dependencies, and verification limits inform recommendations; the rubric is not RICE, numeric weights, or a deterministic queue. Recommendations do not authorize changes.

nodes.label: Recorded policy adoption
nodes.rationale: Authorship alone does not establish policy. Recorded maintainer proposal or adoption distinguishes new-by-policy from new-user-request; retaining both labels preserves outside-demand evidence.

nodes.label: Re-engineering
nodes.rationale: A change to observable behavior or an explicit developer-facing contract is re-engineering, even if it also restructures internals. Keep classifications in separate commits, potentially within one cohesive PR.

nodes.label: Refactoring
nodes.rationale: Internal structure may change, but observable behavior and explicit contracts must remain. Tests are evidence rather than the definition; incidental setup may change without weakening behavioral or negative coverage.

nodes.label: RFC 2119 analysis naming
nodes.rationale: Convention-folder names express Must, MustNot, Should, ShouldNot, or optional Can semantics; shared PHPCSSniff and PHPStanRule filenames and eightfold identifiers retain convention identity.

nodes.label: Explicit boolean negation
nodes.rationale: Prefer positive conditions or strict true/false comparisons, preserving evaluation order and short-circuiting. Unknown or nullable operands need intent review because strict comparison is not equivalent to truthiness negation.

nodes.label: Efqs PHPCS registration shell delegation
nodes.rationale: Convention-specific PHPCSSniff bodies are exposed through Eightfold Efqs category registration shells; namespace and Sniff suffix determine diagnostic codes. Explicit sniff tests still analyze fixtures excluded from style sweeps.

nodes.label: Fixture–test–implementation–activation approval flow
nodes.rationale: Fixture, test, and activation approvals are separate gates. Valid failing assertions must precede implementation; setup errors are not red tests. Preserve intentional fixture violations and report unrelated baseline failures.

nodes.label: Evidence-based completion
nodes.rationale: Completion requires actual edits and status/diff evidence; analysis alone is not delivery. Report untracked, deleted, and renamed paths as well as tracked diffs.

nodes.label: Guidance is not enforcement
nodes.rationale: Written rules do not prove tool enforcement and do not authorize repository-wide refactoring.

nodes.label: Human-controlled authorization gates
nodes.rationale: Opening a new PR and merging require explicit authorization; updating an existing session PR does not. Recommendations do not themselves authorize repository or issue changes.

nodes.label: Impersonal voice
nodes.rationale: Center work and reality rather than ownership or blame; possessive acknowledgment remains appropriate for giving credit.

nodes.label: One canonical home per fact
nodes.rationale: Linked paraphrases must preserve canonical meaning; report drift and record local adaptations in the agent context rather than silently moving established information.

nodes.label: Graphify artifact-tracking baseline
nodes.rationale: Commit graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, and graph.html for immediately queryable checkouts; ignore caches, metrics, manifests, checkout paths, and dated snapshots. Keep backups unless committed artifacts and explicit project policy adopt Git recovery.

nodes.label: Graphify code-only CLI refresh
nodes.rationale: graphify update . and code-only post-merge hooks update code but cannot substitute for semantic extraction after documentation changes.

nodes.label: Agent-hosted Graphify semantic refresh
nodes.rationale: The skill refreshes code and prose without an external LLM key. Success requires regenerated graph/report, a saved manifest, changed-document extraction accounting, and warning/usage disclosure; preserve and mark stale graphs after partial failures.

nodes.label: Measured versus unavailable extraction usage
nodes.rationale: Report semantic token counts only when exposed by the host; placeholder zeros are not measurements. Report PHP 8.5 parser gaps instead of rewriting valid source or suppressing warnings.

nodes.label: Unsupported callable inference design material
nodes.rationale: Drafts remain non-autoloaded, outside the supported PHPUnit suite, and cannot run as-is due to missing types, mismatched signatures, undeclared enum cases, an unimplemented rule, and a fixture parse error. Contracts and behavior need design and tests before support.

nodes.label: Efqs reusable-file copy commands
nodes.rationale: Commands copy package-relative sources to identical consumer-relative destinations, create directories, leave identical files unchanged, and refuse different-file overwrites. Copying neither installs tooling/labels nor adopts consumer-specific facts.

nodes.label: Method Scope Conventions for self, static, parent, and this
nodes.norm_label: method scope conventions for self, static, parent, and this

nodes.label: Adapter
nodes.rationale: Wrapping the target class inside a dedicated adapter class is the recommended alternative.

nodes.label: Constructor injection (composition)
nodes.rationale: Inject an instance via the constructor as a composition alternative.

nodes.label: PHP trait (horizontal composition)
nodes.rationale: Move shared behavior into a PHP trait for horizontal composition.

nodes.label: Attribute alternative to avoiding subclassing
nodes.rationale: Class decoration with the attribute supplied by {{attributeName}} is offered as an alternative to {{mustTip}}; the concrete attribute is not named.

nodes.label: Guard / assertion method pattern
nodes.rationale: AuthorizationGuard demonstrates fail-closed checks and PHP 8.5 NoDiscard to prevent silently ignoring critical authorization results; the example depends on application-provided SecurityContext.

nodes.label: Terminal handler pattern
nodes.rationale: AccountDashboardHandler is a single-responsibility terminal pipeline entry that produces the final response without downstream delegation.

nodes.label: Middleware interceptor pattern
nodes.rationale: MfaVerificationMiddleware accepts context and a downstream handler, short-circuiting failed MFA or delegating request processing.

nodes.label: Property hook accessor pattern
nodes.rationale: UserProfile demonstrates backed set-hook validation and normalization plus a virtual computed fullName, encapsulating property invariants without generic magic methods.

nodes.label: Permission voter pattern
nodes.rationale: AdminRoleVoter evaluates permissions without mutating context and returns explicit Granted, Denied, or Abstain votes.

nodes.label: Mozilla Code of Conduct Enforcement Ladder
nodes.norm_label: mozilla code of conduct enforcement ladder

nodes.label: Major, Minor, and Patch Compatibility Meanings
nodes.norm_label: major, minor, and patch compatibility meanings

nodes.label: Explicit false comparison for boolean operands
nodes.norm_label: explicit false comparison for boolean operands
nodes.rationale: Replace !expression with expression === false only for a boolean operand, preserving grouping and short-circuiting.

nodes.label: Attribute alternative to final declaration
nodes.rationale: Class decoration with the attribute supplied by {{attributeName}} is offered as an alternative to {{mustTip}}; the concrete attribute is not named.

nodes.label: Final concrete classes by default
nodes.rationale: Concrete classes should be final; non-final extension points require an explicit BaseClass attribute with non-empty rationale.

nodes.label: InstanceMethodsMustNotBeAccessedViaThis
nodes.rationale: The diagnostic prohibits using $this to access a method.

nodes.label: Analysis baseline
nodes.rationale: The documented pre-existing baseline includes PHPCS line-length warnings and PHPStan errors because PHPCS's autoloader is not loaded by default, plus additional test and fixture type errors when it is loaded. Custom PHPStan registrations are commented out; unrelated code should not be fixed as part of other work.

nodes.label: Analysis layout
nodes.rationale: Convention implementations live under src/Analysis/<Convention> and expose PHPStanRule.php and PHPCSSniff.php. PHPCS registration shells under src/PHPCS/Efqs delegate to convention implementations. Analysis tests and PHPStan and PHPCS fixtures have separate test directories; experiments are outside Composer autoloading.

nodes.label: Boolean negation rule
nodes.rationale: The disabled BooleanNegationMustBeExplicit PHPStan rule reports unary ! when PHPStan knows the operand is boolean, using non-ignorable identifier eightfold.booleanNegationMustBeExplicit. Nullable, non-boolean, and unknown operands need manual intent review; isolated fixture tests do not imply repository activation.

nodes.label: Composer graph code
nodes.rationale: composer graph:code, also available as composer graph:refresh, refreshes code in an existing graph using graphify update . without an agent or API key. It searches PATH and ~/.local/bin for the CLI and fails on a missing graph, missing CLI, or update failure. Documentation changes still need semantic refresh.

nodes.label: Composer quality checks
nodes.rationale: composer check runs style, analysis, and tests; composer check:instructions separately checks path-specific instruction coverage. composer production runs check and optimizes the autoloader. composer local currently only runs check despite its aspirational description.

nodes.label: Convention PR exception
nodes.rationale: The local adaptation to the shared pull-request gate lets a convention-development request authorize opening a pull request containing the initial fixture-only draft without separate approval. Later stages retain the convention workflow's approval gates.

nodes.label: Diagnostic templates
nodes.rationale: Convention diagnostics use named Markdown templates compiled by PHP with {{placeholder}} substitution. Missing templates and unresolved placeholders raise explicit errors, and templates are not cached.

nodes.label: Custom PHPStan rules disabled by default
nodes.norm_label: custom phpstan rules disabled by default
nodes.rationale: PHPCS style, built-in and vendor PHPStan analysis, and PHPUnit are enforced through Composer checks. All custom PHPStan rule registrations are disabled in extension.neon; isolated fixture tests can still run. AGENTS.md guidance is not enforced unless a tool or check implements it.

nodes.label: Graph policy
nodes.rationale: The knowledge graph exists, its workflow guide applies, and updating it needs no separate approval. Core graph artifacts are committed; local-only Graphify files are listed in .gitignore.

nodes.label: Information hierarchy adaptation
nodes.rationale: The information hierarchy points to 8fold/site-masteringthemundane.com at bc4f99d until this package ships its own copy.

nodes.label: Path-specific instruction coverage check
nodes.rationale: composer check:instructions lists tracked files matched by each instruction applyTo pattern and fails for missing or malformed frontmatter or patterns matching no tracked files. Review output for missing or unexpected matches; the repository-only CLI is the canonical source for glob semantics, scopes, limits, and exit codes.

nodes.label: Local runtime
nodes.rationale: The project declares PHP ^8.5. The documented local environment uses MAMP PHP 8.5.2 at /Applications/MAMP/bin/php/php8.5.2/bin/php, a path not assumed elsewhere; no secret templates, directed secret copies, or local preview are specified.

nodes.label: Repository scope
nodes.rationale: 8fold/php-architecture is the canonical home of the shared agent–user rules and a complete PHP library; its repository context and ignore configuration are baselines for consuming projects. The library has no web server, preview, database, or secret environment setup.

nodes.label: Session startup
nodes.rationale: First check and refresh the knowledge graph under the local policy before reading other documents. Then read AGENTS.md and the agent context and check the branch and git status.

nodes.label: Activation approval
nodes.rationale: Review implementation and results and obtain separate explicit approval before enabling the convention in repository analysis. Follow layer-specific integration and validation, reporting unrelated baseline violations without expanding scope.

nodes.label: Agent instruction layer
nodes.rationale: Every convention needs agent guidance, in a new or existing path-specific instruction that passes composer check:instructions.

nodes.label: Convention request
nodes.rationale: The workflow starts when a user asks for a convention or agent instruction, or an issue requests one. Exhaustive agreement on names, exceptions, and ordering is not required before drafting fixtures.

nodes.label: Fixture approval
nodes.rationale: Present fixtures and iterate with the user until they represent the intended convention; resolve scope questions through concrete examples. Obtain explicit fixture approval before writing tests. Fixture approval authorizes tests, not implementation.

nodes.label: Fixture draft
nodes.rationale: Draft syntactically valid compliant and intentionally noncompliant fixtures in the applicable analyzer's fixture directory. Describe expected diagnostics, cases that must not be reported, and provisional assumptions.

nodes.label: Fixture-first development
nodes.rationale: Develop a requested convention from the closest reasonable approximations of compliant and noncompliant PHP code and refine them through review instead of requiring a complete abstract specification first.

nodes.label: Fixture-only PR exception
nodes.rationale: A request to develop a convention authorizes opening a pull request containing the initial fixture-only draft for review without separate approval under the usual pull-request gate. It does not authorize tests, implementation, or activation.

nodes.label: Implementation
nodes.rationale: Implement approved behavior until the approved tests pass; do not weaken assertions or repair intentional fixture violations merely to make tests pass.

nodes.label: Shared contract interface layer
nodes.rationale: An interface is optional when a shared contract supports the convention and its benefit outweighs its cost.

nodes.label: Issue tracking
nodes.rationale: Track all layers in one issue using the convention request template and retaining its sections; update an existing issue rather than duplicating it. Issue creation is not required to draft fixtures and does not authorize implementation. Separate issues per layer require a user request.

nodes.label: Layer assessment
nodes.rationale: Assess every layer while refining fixtures, including alternatives and reasons to skip a layer. If a layer lacks an automated test or activation step, record why that stage does not apply; recommend optional work only when benefits outweigh costs.

nodes.label: Layer selection criteria
nodes.rationale: Weigh accuracy and false positives, overlapping existing or third-party rules, impact on existing code and possible Should severity or a baseline, and whether a suggested fix preserves behavior. Guidance is not permission to refactor existing code.

nodes.label: PHPCS token-analysis layer
nodes.rationale: A PHPCS sniff applies when tokens alone can detect a convention; PHPCS cannot see types. Consider whether detection is precise enough and whether its benefit outweighs its cost.

nodes.label: PHPStan semantic-analysis layer
nodes.rationale: Use a PHPStan rule when detection needs types, symbols, or semantic analysis. No separate process is documented yet, so follow the sniff stages and identical approval gates.

nodes.label: Test approval
nodes.rationale: Review assertions and observed results with the user, iterate, and obtain explicit approval before implementation. Test approval does not authorize activation.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.rationale: After fixture approval, write isolated tests for agreed analyzer behavior and demonstrate the intended failing assertions before implementation. Follow the relevant layer's diagnostic-assertion and setup process.

nodes.label: Shared implementation trait layer
nodes.rationale: A trait is optional when shared implementation supports the convention and its benefit outweighs its cost.
